title: Capacity sprint: routing adjustments & deprioritization notes
content:
Weekly catch-up capture: informal notes, hypotheses, and action items from the 11/29 capacity sprint huddle. Purpose: converge on a routing + deprioritization approach for the next 2-week sprint that reduces tail-risk in EMEA/Edge while keeping latency SLOs for hosted API top-tier customers.

TL;DR
- We observed sustained 18% edge demand growth in the past 10 days concentrated in APAC micro-regions; current buffer rules under-provision these zones.
- Proposed short-term: soft-deprioritization band for non-urgent Dedicated bursts + route non-critical inference to cost-tier model variants (int8 / smaller context).
- Immediate experiments: enable regional prewarming for 3 high-variance zones (SIN, HKG, MUM) and gate incoming queued requests with new priority header.

Observed signals this week:
- 11/25–11/28: APAC edge QPS +18% (moving average), 95th latency up 220ms vs baseline in SIN and HKG.
- Preemption events increased 2.4x on mid-tier GPU pools (mixed T4/RTX stacks) when bursts overlap with Dedicated maintenance windows.
- Cost bump noted: opportunistic spill -> fallback to larger cross-region instances created extra egress and inter-region placement (~$0.9k/day for last 72h).
- Canary metric: dropped success ratio for embeddings-critical path for one alpha customer to 98.3% (SLO 99.5%).

Hypotheses / constraints:
- Hotspots look less like true model compute demand and more like concentrated test harnesses + chatbots with high-concurrency. If we can detect synthetic-like patterns we can apply stricter backpressure.
- We must not degrade 99th latency for platinum tier customers; any deprioritization must be transparent and reversible.
- Private deployments cannot be routed off-region; deprioritization only available for hosted/dedicated customers.

Routing proposals (short list):
1) Priority header + admission control (P0/P1/P2)
   - P0: platinum SLA (no deprioritization)
   - P1: standard (eligible for smaller-variant fallback)
   - P2: background / experimental (eligible for queuing + deprioritization)
   - Implementation note: token-level billing unchanged, but route chooses int8-quantized variant when P1 and latency budget allows.

2) Regional prewarm for top-3 high-variance zones for 72-hour windows
   - Prewarm budget: allocate 5% of regional spare capacity purely for prewarming; auto-release after window.
   - Measure: priming latency samples and warm-KV hits. Success threshold: >60% warm-hit at 95th percentile token latency reduction of 120ms.

3) Deprioritization schedule + safety gating
   - Deprioritization only allowed during declared surge windows or when regional health index < 0.85.
   - Circuit-breaker: if any P0 route sees degradation > 1% error rate, immediately cancel deprioritization and trigger fallback route.

Experiment matrix (next 14 days):
- Exp A: Priority header rollout (canary 5% traffic to APAC edge) — owner Arjun (INFRA-4217). Success if no P0 degradation and P1 latency reduces tail by 10% under same load.
- Exp B: Prewarm pool for SIN/HKG/MUM — owner Lena. Metrics: warm-hit, cost/day, 95th token latency delta.
- Exp C: Heuristic backpressure to detect synthetic harnesses (burst pattern detection) — owner Diego. False-positive rate must be <2% in internal tests.

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- (Arjun) Implement priority-header passthrough in router and admission control stub — prototype by 2029-12-03.
- (Lena) Script for automated regional prewarm allocation + auto-release — finish smoke tests by 2029-12-05.
- (Diego) Build burst-detection classifier (simple histogram/threshold first) and integrate with admission control; demo 2029-12-04.
- (Priya) Cost monitoring dashboard for cross-region spill and prewarm spend; initial tiles by 2029-12-06.
- (Maya) Draft customer communication plan for deprioritization (FAQ + opt-out) and coordinate with CS — first draft 2029-12-07.

Open questions / risks:
- Billing implications for customers routed to smaller variants: should token pricing change if we fallback to quantized model? Legal and billing teams need to weigh. (flagged to Finance).
- Edge private deployments: How to signal deprioritization at control plane without violating VPC constraints? Needs security review.
- Warm-up budget tradeoff: holding spare capacity reduces available opportunistic capacity — need run-rate model to justify.

Notes from quick infra review:
- Node churn in SIN region peaked early Thursday; logs point to a multi-tenant host kernel update combined with a scheduling bug (K8s descheduler). Patch landed in staging; SRE to monitor for 48h.
- Autoscaler sensitivity: current scale-down cool-down is 5m which may be too aggressive for prewarm strategy; propose 15m for prewarm-tagged pools.

Customer impact summary (for comms):
- Most customers unaffected; small set of high-concurrency test tenants might see increased queuing or fall back to smaller-variant model.
- Platinum customers: guaranteed no routing change; will be used to validate circuit-breaker.

Meeting notes (who said what, shorthand):
- Arjun: "priority header is low-friction, gives us knob without wholesale infra changes".
- Lena: "prewarm works but we need auto-release otherwise costs balloon".
- Diego: "burst heuristics must be cheap — don't want heavy ML in the hot path".
- Priya: "we need signals and concrete translation for billing, CS will get questions".

Next sync: Thursday 12/05 10:00 PT — focus: demo priority-header canary + first prewarm smoke test results.

Notes-to-self / rough checklist:
- make sure to tag test traffic via header 'x-rw-priority' for telemetry filters
- add log field 'fallback_variant' to token billing traces
- add 'prewarm_tag' in infra metadata and link to pool-id
- schedule quick legal and finance sync (15m) after we have baseline cost numbers

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Global QPS (11/22–11/28): baseline 34k -> current 41k (20% week delta)
- APAC-edge QPS share: 12% -> 14.5%
- Regional spare capacity (unallocated): EMEA 8.4% | APAC 3.1% | NA 12.2%
- 95th latency (SIN): baseline 480ms -> current 720ms

If anything here looks like it belongs in runbook proper, call it out and I'll promote the text. This doc is intentionally a working capture — expect iterated versions next week.
